intro: Lesson 67: Isosceles and equilateral triangles. To understand how the properties of isosceles and equilateral triangles help find missing angles

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 72°. Find the other two angles.
questions.model: The other base angle is also 72°. 180 - 72 - 72 = 36°.

questions.q: Find each angle of an isosceles right-angled triangle.
An isosceles triangle has angles x, x and 2x. Find x.

(a) Isosceles, top angle 34°: the base angles? (b) Isosceles, base angle 49°: the top angle? (c) Equilateral triangle ABC with BC extended to D: angle ACD? (d) Isosceles with base angles (2y + 10)° and top angle 80°: find y.
questions.model: (a) 180 - 34 = 146; 146 ÷ 2 = 73° each (base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal; angles in a triangle add up to 180°).

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 40°. Find both possible sets of angles.
In triangle PQR, PQ = PR and angle P = 44°. QR is extended to S. Find angle PRS, giving reasons.
questions.a: Base angles (180 - 44) ÷ 2 = 68°; PRS = 180 - 68 = 112° (angles on a straight line)

questions.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is:
Isosceles, top angle 100°: the base angles?
Big question: if two sides are equal, what must be true about the angles?
questions.a: The two angles opposite the equal sides (the base angles) are equal.
